title: Welcome Muse Spark Open: open-weight frontier multimodal mixture-of-experts model from Meta
gist: Hugging Face announces Meta's Muse Spark Open, an open-weight multimodal MoE model (~816B total, ~42B active, 1M context) trained for agentic coding, and documents inference paths (transformers, llama.cpp, SGLang, vLLM, MLX, Inference Endpoints), a TRL LoRA fine-tune and agentic demos. Deployment needs very large memory despite 42B-active compute.

insights.claim: Muse Spark Open is an open-weight multimodal mixture-of-experts model with approximately 816B total parameters, about 42B active per token and a context window of up to 1M tokens, taking text, images, audio and video as input and generating text.
insights.speaker: Pedro Cuenca
insights.so_what: Sets a new scale bar for US open-weight models; track adoption versus closed frontier models.
insights.quote: the most capable US open-weights model to date

insights.claim: Each of the 62 layers routes every token to 8 of 256 experts, and the experts hold about 97% of parameters, so compute per token is that of a ~42B model while memory must hold all 816B parameters.
insights.speaker: Pedro Cuenca
insights.so_what: Inference economics favor throughput but memory capacity (not FLOPs) is the binding constraint for deployers.
insights.quote: deployment needs the memory of an 816B-parameter model, but runs at the much faster speed of a 42B model

insights.claim: The model is the full-size member of Meta's Muse series, following the small dense Muse Glimmer released in August; both share a tokenizer and vocabulary, and Muse Spark Open adds an audio encoder that Glimmer lacks.
insights.speaker: Pedro Cuenca
insights.so_what: Meta is running a tiered open-weight family strategy, small local model plus large frontier-class model.

insights.claim: Grouped-query attention (16 KV heads, 62 layers) keeps the KV cache at about 250 KB per token, roughly 266 GB for a full 1M-token context in BF16.
insights.speaker: Pedro Cuenca
insights.so_what: Full-context serving adds a large memory bill on top of weights, limiting practical context length on commodity hardware.

insights.claim: Meta trained the model for agentic coding on real developer workflows such as multi-file refactors and long debugging sessions, with planning, acting, observing and self-correcting loops including web browsing with images.
insights.speaker: Pedro Cuenca
insights.so_what: Positions an open model against closed coding agents; watch coding-agent benchmarks and adoption.
insights.quote: Meta describes Muse Spark Open as a coding-optimized model trained on real developer workflows

insights.claim: Reasoning cannot be turned off in Muse Spark Open; the default is xhigh and users must set effort to low to spend fewer tokens on easy tasks, with levels mapping to integers 16, 64, 256 and 512.
insights.speaker: Pedro Cuenca
insights.so_what: Token cost per request is structurally higher; budget for reasoning overhead in agent loops.
insights.quote: turning off reasoning is not possible with Muse Spark Open

insights.claim: The model uses a Harmony-style channel-based chat template first introduced by gpt-oss, routing to self (reasoning), commentary, user and tool recipients.
insights.speaker: Pedro Cuenca
insights.so_what: Template convergence across vendors eases tool-calling interoperability.

insights.claim: The BF16 checkpoint is about 1.5 TB and runs across 4 nodes of 8 H200 GPUs in transformers, while the NVFP4 4-bit checkpoint, claimed to have negligible accuracy loss, runs on a single B200 node and is targeted at NVIDIA Blackwell.
insights.speaker: Pedro Cuenca
insights.so_what: Blackwell-native 4-bit formats make frontier-scale open models servable on a single node, supporting NVIDIA demand.

insights.claim: On a Mac M3 Ultra with 512 GB, a 2-bit llama.cpp quant runs at 18 tokens/s using 304 GB, and an oMLX 3-bit quant uses about 344 GB at roughly 225 tok/s prefill and 21 tok/s generation.
insights.speaker: Pedro Cuenca
insights.so_what: High-memory Apple silicon is a viable local host for frontier-size open models, albeit slowly.

insights.claim: Hugging Face Inference Endpoints offers a pre-validated SGLang recipe for the NVFP4 variant on 8 RTX Pro 6000 98GB GPUs with 131,072 context or 8 H200 141GB GPUs for the full 1,048,576 context.
insights.speaker: Pedro Cuenca
insights.so_what: Shows concrete GPU bill of materials for managed hosting of the model.
insights.locator: Deploying Muse Spark Open with Inference Endpoints

insights.claim: Launch-day inference support spans transformers, llama.cpp, SGLang, vLLM and MLX, though the vLLM reference integration supports only text and image inputs and needs Blackwell GPUs.
insights.speaker: Pedro Cuenca
insights.so_what: Broad day-zero ecosystem support reduces adoption friction for open weights.

insights.claim: A LoRA SFT on attention projections with frozen experts across 8 nodes of 8 H100s (64 GPUs, FSDP plus expert parallelism) ran 500 steps in about 2 hours at ~8,000 tokens/s, raising mean token accuracy from 72% to 84% and cutting loss from 1.26 to 0.57.
insights.speaker: Pedro Cuenca
insights.so_what: Fine-tuning an 816B model requires a 64-GPU cluster even with frozen experts, a cost barrier for most teams.

insights.claim: Hugging Face reports being amazed at the model's computer-use performance and built demos (a Pi coding agent generating Three.js assets, an OpenEnv browser agent using only screenshots, and a voice-driven Amazon shopping agent), though the article gives no benchmark scores.
insights.speaker: Pedro Cuenca
insights.so_what: Qualitative only; wait for independent benchmark results before drawing capability conclusions.
insights.quote: We tested Spark on computer use tasks and were amazed by the performance
